attribution_limitations: The discussion states that all patients ingested more than 20 mL of 24% PQ; for this patient the case text gives about 20 mL, which does not literally conflict, but the same sentence is contradicted for the other three patients, so it is kept as a review-only ambiguous fact (p1-f063) and the case-text dose stays included.

Two sentences place the chest radiograph findings differently: an unspecified subsequent radiograph after the first 24 h shows bilateral lower-lobe and perihilar infiltration, and the Day 3 radiograph shows bilateral infiltrates with pneumomediastinum and pneumopericardium.

patients.label: 35-year-old woman who ingested paraquat with suicidal intent and recovered after 19 days (Case II)
attribution_limitations: The amount is 20 mL in the case text but the discussion says all patients ingested more than 20 mL of 24% PQ; only the amount is quarantined (p2-f066 and p2-f005), while the ingestion and its timing stay included (p2-f004).

On the fourth day an unnamed vasopressor is said to have been stopped subsequently, and the same paragraph says vasopressin therapy was continued; the text never says the stopped vasopressor is the vasopressin, so both statements are kept as written.

The route of ondansetron and fluids, and of N-acetylcysteine and vitamin C, is not stated separately from the word intravenous that precedes the first drug in each list. The discussion gives a vitamin C dose (1 g intravenously twice daily) for "our cases" without naming which patients; it is not assigned to this patient.

The sentence saying they were quickly taken to Hetauda Hospital before referral does not state who they were; the elder son paragraph says he was taken to a nearby hospital along with his mother and brother.

patients.label: 7-year-old boy given paraquat in milk by his mother who recovered after 8 days (elder son in Case II)
attribution_limitations: Whether and how much paraquat this child ingested is described inconsistently: the abstract says he ingested paraquat mixed with milk, the case text says he spat it out due to the bitter taste, and the discussion says all patients ingested more than 20 mL of 24% PQ. The spat-out and more-than-20-mL statements conflict and are both review-only (p3-f008, p3-f007); the exposure itself stays included.

The exposure is given as 3 h prior to ER presentation, and the same paragraph says the exact time since ingestion was unclear when the child was found; an approximate interval and an unknown exact time are compatible, so the 3 h interval is kept on the included exposure fact. The referral from the nearby hospital is described as after 3.5 h without naming its starting point.
The fragment "3 h prior to ER presentation" follows the exposure sentence after a stray full stop; it is read as the time of that exposure.

Paragraphs b00019 and b00024 (and b00020 and b00025) repeat the PICU and discharge sentences with slightly different wording (mild cough versus dry cough); they are recorded once per fact with both segments cited.

patients.label: 1-year-old infant with developmental delay, dystonia and seizure disorder given paraquat in milk who died 7 hours after admission (younger son in Case II)
attribution_limitations: The amount is approximately 5 mL (around 100 mg/kg) in the case text, whereas the discussion says all patients ingested more than 20 mL of 24% PQ; both amount facts are review-only source-conflict facts, while the ingestion and its timing stay included (p4-f005).

The paragraph describing the seizure, cyanosis, intubation, bradycardia and death (b00027) says "the child" without naming the younger son. It follows the younger-son paragraph (b00026) that shifts "the child" to the PICU, and its 7 h after admission death matches the abstract statement about the 1-year-old infant; the elder son was discharged after 8 days.
The abstract says the infant presented with acute respiratory distress and neurological impairment; the case text lists stridor, unstable airway, hypertonia and dystonia without those exact labels.

The mother's fourth-day statements (an unnamed vasopressor stopped; vasopressin continued) do not name the same drug, so both are kept as included facts with an ambiguity.

The discussion vitamin C dose (1 g intravenously twice daily, "in our cases"), the fulminant category (stated as following from the more-than-20-mL sentence that the case text contradicts), antioxidant benefit and survival statements are series-level and are not copied to individuals.
Several narrative paragraphs (b00019 and b00024, b00020 and b00025) repeat the elder son sentences; each fact cites both segments once.
